ci: GitHub Pages (landing page, flash/RAM/speed history), Doxygen and CodeQL for Mk2_1phase_RFdatalog_temp (#29)

* ci: GitHub Pages landing page and flash/RAM/speed history

Port of the PVRouter-3-phase pages: a pages job in build.yml (push to dev) appends the
sizes of every build and the embedded benchmarks to bench/history.json of gh-pages with
scripts/ci/pages_update.py, and publishes pages/ (landing page, charts), without the
configurator. build.yml is now valid UTF-8 (a cp1252 micro sign and em dash had slipped in).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: Doxygen to doc/ and CodeQL follow Mk2_1phase_RFdatalog_temp

doxygen-gh-pages.yml as in PVRouter-3-phase: Doxygen 1.13.2 deployed to doc/ of gh-pages,
in the gh-pages concurrency group, on pushes to main touching the firmware or the Doxyfile.
The root Doxyfile takes the firmware as INPUT, its @mainpage as main page. CodeQL builds the
firmware (and dev/ projects) with PlatformIO, plus the actions and python languages.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: flash and RAM badges, links to the pages, changelog

f_voltageCalOldBoard 0.805653, as in Mk2_fasterControl_Full (the voltage

feat: the shipped config.h has one load, on D5 (#31)

* feat: the shipped config.h has one load, on D5

Most single-phase users have a single water heater. config.h now ships with
NO_OF_DUMPLOADS{ 1 }, Load::local(5) and priorities { 0 }; its comments show
what to change for a second and a third load (D6, D7). Users keeping their own
config.h are unaffected.

The grid simulator keeps three loads: sim_config.sh calls the new
sim/configs/three_loads.sh, which the CI builds that apply a patch without
sim_config.sh (remote loads, SEG_HW) and measure.sh run first. The patches'
hunks move down by the seven comment lines. The compile-fail cases that need
more than one load set them with a new loads helper; case 03 builds the three
loads of the comment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(configurator): the three single-phase boards, the display and their pins

- model: displayPins() (display_core.h pinsOf(), A0..A5 as 14..19),

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(configurator): CT2, the diverted energy

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(configurator): calibration helper for the single-phase boards and CT2

The helper reads and rewrites the scalars of the single-phase calibration.h,
one set per board:
- OLD_SEG, OLD_OLED: f_powerCalOldBoard, f_powerCalDivertedOldBoard and
  f_voltageCalOldBoard, each corrected by its reading (P:, diverted, V:);
- NEW: f_ctRating and f_ctRatingDiverted as entered, f_powerCalPerAmp and
  f_voltageCalNewBoard corrected. CT2 has no factor of its own there: the
  diverted reading is a check, and from 5 % of error left after the grid
  correction the page suggests checking f_ctRatingDiverted.

Without CT2, no diverted reading and no CT2 line. calibrationArray becomes
calibrationToken / calibrationValue; a save with per-phase arrays loads
without them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(configurator): single-phase page, switch to the 3-phase one, saves of the other router refused

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(configurator): CT2 on the new board corrects f_ctRatingDiverted

As the router's Readme says (calibration, step 4): on the new board the
diverted reading corrects f_ctRatingDiverted, net of the grid correction
that f_powerCalPerAmp, shared by CT2, already takes:
  new f_ctRatingDiverted = old x kD / kGrid
with kGrid = 1 when the grid correction does not apply. f_ctRating is still
never corrected. The CT2 check (divertedError, warn.calCt2) goes.

Also, from the review of the single-phase page: the message of a refused
save goes after a good load or a reset, follows a language change, and its
box is centred.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(configurator): CT ratings written with 3 decimals

f_ctRatingDiverted is now a corrected value, and f_ctRating a typed one
such as 4.44 (666 / 150 ohms): with 1 decimal, the rounding could reach
1 %, as large as the corrections. Both are written with 3 decimals, on
the page and in calibration.h. A value left unchanged, or giving the same
text, keeps the bytes of the file (50.0F stays 50.0F).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(configurator): single-phase presets, CI and Pages preview

Five presets (old boards with their displays, remote units with relays and dual tariff,
mk2Wifi inputs, 60 Hz), a Configurator CI job, the configurator preview in the Pages job,
the READMEs, landing page and CHANGELOG, and the shipped config.h pointing to the
single-phase page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(configurator): pin uses named in the page's language

The pin errors named their users in English ("load 1", "temperature"),

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(configurator): pin lists no longer offer the RF chip's pins

With the RFM69 present, D2 and D10 to D13 were offered and then refused

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(configurator): CT ratings without trailing zeros, 50.0F stays 50.0F

The CT ratings were written with 3 decimals even when round (50.000F where
calibration.h has 50.0F). Their trailing zeros are now dropped, one decimal
kept: 4.44F, 40.909F, 50.0F. The page's preview uses the same format.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style: receiver job lines split again, CHANGELOG entries wrapped

The copy of the receiver job had lost its line continuations. The new

refactor: the ADC set up in two register writes, each bit named once (#34)

Port of PVRouter-3-phase#255. ADCSRA (0x7A, outside the sbi/cbi range) was
built with eight volatile read-modify-writes; it is now cleared, then
written once with ADEN, ADSC (allowed together), ADATE, ADIE and the /128
prescaler. Same register values; 26 bytes less flash locally. Simulator
verdicts unchanged against dev. CLAUDE.md: every change is ported to the
3-phase firmware when it applies.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf: one write per port for the load pins, and only on the ports they use (#35)

* perf: one write per port for the load pins, and only on the ports they use

The ports are volatile, so setPinsOFF() then setPinsON() read and wrote
PORTD and PORTB twice each per ADC interrupt, PORTB included when no load
pin is on it (mask 0). setPinsState<usedPins>(on, off) writes each port
once, and only the ports a load pin is on, decided at compile time from
the load map (getLoadPins(): TRIAC pins and remote-load status LEDs).

Ported from PVRouter-3-phase (same change).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: the startup pin setup skips the ports none of its pins is on

setPinsAsOutput() and setPinsAsInputPullup() take their pins as a
template argument: DDRB |= 0 or PORTB |= 0 is still a read and a write on
a volatile register, now a port without any of the pins is not touched.
12 bytes less with the default configuration.

The remote load receiver gets the new utils_pins.h (CI checks that its
copy matches) and calls setPinsState() instead of setPinsOFF().

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sim): input pins read their scripted level at once

simavr copies the external levels set with AVR_IOCTL_IOPORT_SET_EXTERNAL
into PINx only when the firmware writes the port. The firmware used to
write PORTB once per mains cycle even without a load pin on it (PORTB
&= ~0, PORTB |= 0), which refreshed PINB by chance; now that it does not,
the inputs on PORTB (rotation D12, relay override D13) were never seen
in the relay scenarios. Each pin of an 'input' line now gets its level
through its IRQ, as the DS18B20 bus already does, so PINx follows the pin
as on the chip.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: the Doxygen documentation follows dev (#37)

The doc was deployed on pushes to main only, so it went stale between
releases and was refreshed by hand from dev, while the size and speed
history next to it follows every push to dev. It is now deployed on each
push to dev that touches the firmware or the Doxyfile; the doc badge and
the landing page say so.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: the CT filter checked in validation.h, runNextCycleTask() a call, doc slips (#38)

- The CT1 filter settings are checked in validation.h with the 3-phase message, whatever the
  board, instead of in processing.cpp, where only an enabled filter was checked; compile-fail
  cases 88-92 (alpha too large or too small, gain of 64 or negative refused, the old-board
  values build), as the 3-phase 70-74.
- runNextCycleTask() is no longer always_inline: it has two callers (the ADC ISR and
  finishCycleTasks()), so it was there twice. Flash -176 bytes; grid simulator: ISR max 500
  cycles (495) on the old board, 447 (443) on the new one, ADMUX written at most 517 (507).
- calibration.h: alpha "from 0.00005 to below 0.0625", as ct_filter.h accepts it.
- shared_var.h: b_newMainsCycle states its own timing (the DATALOG_SUM cycle task).
- The history of the .ino: the October 2019 entry is the 3-phase sketch, Mk2_3phase_RFdatalog_temp.
- test/README.md: every test folder in the tree and the table (ten were missing), and the right
  firmware name.
- CLAUDE.md: the cycle tasks are in "What differs", and why they are not ported.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix!: the datalog period at most 30 s, its power summed in 32 bits (#40)

No 64-bit arithmetic on the ATmega328P: the power of the datalog period is
summed in 32 bits again, scaled down by 16 when the period needs it, as
V^2 already was. Port of FredM67/PVRouter-3-phase#259.

- Datalog::powerShift() (as in the 3-phase firmware): in ADC steps, a
  full-span sine averages 2^17 per sample; while the sample sets of the
  period times 2^17 fit in 31 bits, no shift, else a shift by 4. With 68
  sets per cycle at most, that is from 5 s on, the default included.
- The shift is applied where each cycle's power is added to the datalog
  sum (addToDatalogSum()), rounded: once per cycle, not per sample, so the
  ISR does not change and the average stays within 1 step^2.
- Datalog::averagePower<SHIFT>(): the average scaled back up, quotient and
  remainder apart, in 32 bits, with a 16- or 32-bit count.
- At most 30 s (validation.h, configurator, Readmes): up to 102600 sample
  sets; the counter keeps widening to 32 bits from 20 s on.
- compile-fail: 31 s refused; 30 s builds at 50 and 60 Hz.

Flash 580 bytes smaller, RAM 8 bytes; ISR unchanged in the simulator.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor: the single-phase code aligned with the 3-phase one (#39)

* fix: the CT filter checked in validation.h, runNextCycleTask() a call, doc slips

- The CT1 filter settings are checked in validation.h with the 3-phase message, whatever the
  board, instead of in processing.cpp, where only an enabled filter was checked; compile-fail
  cases 88-92 (alpha too large or too small, gain of 64 or negative refused, the old-board
  values build), as the 3-phase 70-74.
- runNextCycleTask() is no longer always_inline: it has two callers (the ADC ISR and
  finishCycleTasks()), so it was there twice. Flash -176 bytes; grid simulator: ISR max 500
  cycles (495) on the old board, 447 (443) on the new one, ADMUX written at most 517 (507).
- calibration.h: alpha "from 0.00005 to below 0.0625", as ct_filter.h accepts it.
- shared_var.h: b_newMainsCycle states its own timing (the DATALOG_SUM cycle task).
- The history of the .ino: the October 2019 entry is the 3-phase sketch, Mk2_3phase_RFdatalog_temp.
- test/README.md: every test folder in the tree and the table (ten were missing), and the right
  firmware name.
- CLAUDE.md: the cycle tasks are in "What differs", and why they are not ported.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: the single-phase code aligned with the 3-phase one (shapes, names, wording, tests)

- processStartUp(phase): the phase starts its sums and its sample count afresh at each of its
  crossings during the start-up period, before the end-of-start-up check, the shape of the
  3-phase fix FredM67/PVRouter-3-phase#258 (one phase here, so no change of behaviour).
- AdcChain::NO_OF_CHANNELS is NO_OF_CONVERSIONS, the 3-phase name.
- The CT1 filter state lives inside the if constexpr that uses it, with the 3-phase comment.
- Wording as in the 3-phase firmware: the ADC reference comment, the cycle budget of the ADC
  interrupt (1664 CPU cycles per call), the start-up comment; the tick of the main code says
  when it comes and why a 1-Wire time slot cannot push an ADMUX write past its deadline.
- sample_sets.h: the generic doc of the 3-phase copy; the file is now the same in both.
- test_ct_filter: the same file and README in both firmwares (the 3-phase set: tracking of
  Robin's float on a step, a sine and noise for several gains and alphas, the valid range of the
  settings; the two single-phase tests were the same checks under other names).
- test_adc_chain: the finer tests of the 3-phase one (order of the chain, ADMUX of each channel,
  channel after next, ADMUX written after, channel by round).

Grid simulator: ISR and ADMUX figures unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: sample_sets.h stays the single-phase one

The 3-phase firmware no longer has it (FredM67/PVRouter-3-phase#259: at 30 s
at most, its counter is 16 bits); only the single-phase counter needs to

The new board: f_ctRating, f_powerCalPerAmp, f_ctRatingDiverted (CT2) and

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore: a shared graphify code graph, rebuilt by the pre-commit hook; a root CLAUDE.md (#45)

* chore: a shared graphify code graph, rebuilt by the pre-commit hook

graphify-out/graph.json is a code-only graphify graph (local AST, no LLM),
as in https://docs.graphify.com/cookbooks/shared-team-graph, set up as in
PVRouter-3-phase (#264 there). The pre-commit hook (framework and plain hook)
rebuilds and stages it on commits that change code, with PYTHONHASHSEED=0,
and skips when graphify is not installed or with GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK=1;
pre-commit.ci skips it. No other hook checks the file. .gitattributes selects
the graphify union merge driver, registered per clone (scripts/README.md);
the rest of graphify-out/ stays ignored. .graphifyignore leaves out the
PlatformIO build output (.pio/).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: a root CLAUDE.md, as in PVRouter-3-phase

Gives Claude Code its bearings in the repository, next to the firmware's own
guide (Mk2_1phase_RFdatalog_temp/CLAUDE.md): what is where, the commands
(firmware, compile-fail checks, grid simulator, configurator) and the rules
(branches, commits, formatting, the ISR budget and how it is measured, pins,
warnings, settings, parity with the 3-phase firmware). It follows the root
CLAUDE.md of PVRouter-3-phase, adapted to this repository: the simulator
targets and limits of the single-phase firmware, its boards, no analysis/.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: refuse a relay filter longer than 255 datalog periods (#46)

* fix: refuse a relay filter longer than 255 datalog periods

The relay engine instantiates EWMA_average< D * 60 / DATALOG_PERIOD_IN_SECONDS >,
whose parameter is a uint8_t: RELAY_FILTER_DELAY{ 25 } built silently with a
count of 44 (a filter under 4 minutes instead of 25). validation.h only
checked the lower bound, and on the RELAY_FILTER_DELAY constant rather than
on the minutes relays carries (MINUTES(...) or the default 10).

RelayEngine::filterDelay() gives that D; validation.h checks both bounds on
it (5 to 255 datalog periods). New compile-fail cases: 22 minutes refused,
21 minutes builds, MINUTES(25) with RELAY_FILTER_DELAY 2 refused, and the
lower bound (2 minutes at 30 s), which had no case. Port of FredM67/PVRouter-3-phase#270.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: the NETWORK_ID comment says 1-250, as validation.h checks

config_rf.h and the configurator's generated config_rf.h said 1-255; the
build and the configurator refuse anything above 250.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(configurator): refuse a relay filter longer than 255 datalog periods

The configurator accepted delays of 1 to 10 minutes and checked only the
lower bound: with a 1 s datalog period, 5 minutes or more (300 periods)
gave a config.h that the build now refuses. New message, EN and FR, and a
test case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: the graphify hook rebuilds a code-only graph from scratch (#47)

`graphify update .` merges into the existing graph.json: the nodes of
deleted code stay, and update also indexes the Markdown files, so the
"code-only" graph grew docs nodes on commits that touched them. The hook
now moves graph.json aside, runs
`PYTHONHASHSEED=0 graphify extract . --code-only`, and restores the
previous graph (exit 1) if the extraction fails or writes an empty file.
The AST cache keeps it to a few seconds. Port of
FredM67/PVRouter-3-phase#267.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
